tasks.q: Which of these lines compares two values rather than storing one?
a: if total == 20 then
total = 20
total = total + 20
print(total)
tasks.fb: A double equals sign asks a question; a single one hands an answer to a variable.

tasks.q: A loop is written as  while lives > 0  but nothing inside it ever changes lives. What happens?
a: The loop never ends
The loop runs exactly once
The loop is skipped altogether
The program stops with a syntax error
tasks.fb: The condition stays True for ever, so the program carries on until something forces it to stop.

tasks.q: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, what is the value of  "7" + "2" ?
a: The string 72
The integer 9
The real number 7.2
An error, because two strings cannot be joined
tasks.fb: Both values are strings, so + joins them end to end instead of adding them together.
Casting to an integer throws the decimal part away completely, so it never rounds up.

tasks.q: A program outputs the first line of a file over and over instead of working through it. Which mistake would cause this?
a: The call to readLine() is outside the loop, so no new line is ever read
The file was opened in append mode
The file was never closed
endOfFile() was tested before the file was opened
tasks.fb: Each readLine() call moves one line further on, so it has to sit inside the loop for the loop to make progress.

tasks.q: A program appends a line to a file, but the line is missing when the file is opened again. What is the most likely reason?
a: The file was never closed, so the last data stayed in the buffer
The line was written to the wrong position in the file
The line was cast to an integer first
Append mode always deletes the newest line
tasks.fb: Closing the file pushes everything still waiting in memory out to secondary storage.

tasks.q: A table called Pupils has the fields Name, Year and Choir. Which query returns the names of pupils who are in Year 10 and in the choir?
a: SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Year = 10 AND Choir = True;
SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Year = 10 OR Choir = True;
SELECT Year, Choir FROM Pupils WHERE Name = 'Year 10';
SELECT Name FROM Pupils LIKE Year = 10 AND Choir = True;
tasks.fb: Both conditions must be True at the same time, and AND is the operator that demands that.

tasks.q: A query that should find every surname beginning with M returns no records at all. Which line is the problem?
a: WHERE Surname = 'M%'
WHERE Surname LIKE 'M%'
SELECT Surname
FROM Pupils
tasks.fb: A pattern containing a wildcard needs LIKE; with = the database hunts for a surname that is literally the two characters M and %.

tasks.q: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, which line reads past the end of  array lane[8] ?
a: print(lane[8])
print(lane[0])
print(lane[7])
print(lane[1])
tasks.fb: Eight elements are numbered 0 to 7, so index 8 is one place past the last one.

tasks.q: A sub-program works out a total correctly, but the main program cannot use the answer. What is missing?
a: A return statement to send the total back
A parameter in the sub-program's definition
A global constant
An extra loop inside the sub-program
tasks.fb: With no return it is a procedure, so the value it worked out is thrown away the moment the sub-program ends.

tasks.q: In the OCR Exam Reference Language, how many different values can  random(0, 7)  return?
tasks.fb: Both ends are included, so 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are all possible: exactly one for each element of an array of eight.

tasks.q: A program sets the seed to the same value every time it starts. What effect does that have?
a: It produces exactly the same sequence of numbers on every run
It produces numbers that are truly random
It stops the generator ever repeating a number
It limits every number to the size of the seed
tasks.fb: A fixed seed makes a run repeatable, which is useful when testing and useless in a game.

tasks.q: Put the steps of the lane draw into the order the program must carry them out.
steps: Read the eight runners' names from the file
Declare an array of eight lanes, all empty
Pick a random lane number from 0 to 7
If that lane is already taken, pick another number
Store the runner's name in the empty lane
Write the finished lane list to a new file
tasks.fb: Set the array up before any drawing happens, and never store a name until you have checked that the lane is free.

tasks.q: Which techniques does the lane draw program need? Select all that apply.
opts: Reading the names in from a file
An array to hold the eight lanes
A loop that repeats until a free lane is found
A range check on the runners' names
correct: Reading the names in from a file
An array to hold the eight lanes
A loop that repeats until a free lane is found
tasks.fb: The names come from a file rather than a database table, and a name has no numerical range to check.

tasks.q: Why must the program check whether a lane is already taken before it stores a name?
a: Each call is independent, so the same lane number could easily come up twice
The array would otherwise run out of memory
random() stops working after eight calls
The file could not be written to afterwards
tasks.fb: Two runners in lane 3 and an empty lane 7 is the classic bug in any draw or shuffle.

info.title: Revision that works
info.text: Cover the bullets at a station, say them out loud from memory, then uncover them and check. Reading them again is much easier, and much less useful, than trying to recall them.

info.title: Two marks, two things
info.text: A two-mark question that says state the difference wants both sides written down. Saying what casting does without saying why it is needed throws away half the marks.

info.title: Say which language
info.text: Answering a code question in Python instead of the OCR Exam Reference Language is fine, but stick to one of them for the whole answer. Mixing print() with endif loses marks because neither language is being followed.

info.title: Three lines, three jobs
info.text: Nearly every SQL mark comes from the same three lines: SELECT for the fields, FROM for the table and WHERE for the records. Write them on separate lines and check each one in turn.

info.title: Trace it on paper
info.text: For any program with a loop, draw a column for each variable and add a new row every time round the loop. Most tracing marks in Paper 2 are won or lost on whether you bothered to do this.

info.title: The top number
info.text: In a question about choosing an element at random, the marks are in the range. An array of eight elements needs a number from 0 to 7, and an 8 anywhere in that answer will cost you.

diagrams.title: Sequence, selection and iteration
diagrams.text: The three constructs again: straight through, jump over, jump back.

diagrams.title: How a query runs
diagrams.text: Rows are filtered by WHERE first, then SELECT picks the columns.

diagrams.title: Index positions
diagrams.text: The index is a position, and the last one is one less than the length.
